cited_details.statement: The framework is most commonly associated with Hinton, Vinyals, and Dean, who formalized the *teacher–student* view in their 2015 paper "Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network" ([arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531)).

Their contribution situated KD not only as a model-compression technique but also as a general learning principle: the student is trained to reproduce the teacher's *soft* predictions, augmented with a temperature-scaled distillation loss, alongside the standard cross-entropy on hard labels ([arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531); [lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation](https://www.lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation)).

Their contribution situated KD not only as a model-compression technique but also as a general learning principle: the student is trained to reproduce the teacher's *soft* predictions, augmented with a temperature-scaled distillation loss, alongside the standard cross-entropy on hard labels ([arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531); [lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation](https://www.lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation)).

A smaller *student* network is then trained on the same data, but its loss function is augmented with a *distillation loss* that encourages the student's outputs to match the teacher's outputs, most commonly the softened class probability distribution, the so-called *soft targets* ([lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation](https://www.lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation); [arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531)).

A smaller *student* network is then trained on the same data, but its loss function is augmented with a *distillation loss* that encourages the student's outputs to match the teacher's outputs, most commonly the softened class probability distribution, the so-called *soft targets* ([lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation](https://www.lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation); [arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531)).

The soft targets carry "dark knowledge" — relative similarities between incorrect classes that are not available from a one-hot label — which acts as a richer supervisory signal than the ground-truth alone ([arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531)).

The distillation loss is typically the Kullback–Leibler divergence between the teacher's and student's temperature-scaled output distributions, optionally combined with the standard cross-entropy on the true labels ([lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation](https://www.lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation)).

used this approach to (i) match the predictive performance of an MNIST ensemble with a single small model, and (ii) substantially improve the acoustic model of a deployed commercial system, demonstrating that distillation is not limited to any single modality ([arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531)).

observe that ensembling "is cumbersome and may be too computationally expensive to allow deployment to a large number of users, especially if the individual models are large neural nets," and build on Caruana's earlier demonstration that the knowledge of an ensemble can be compressed into a single model ([arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531)).

**Lightweight deployment under resource constraints.** KD produces a "fast, lightweight" model "suitable" for limited hardware "with minimal accuracy loss," making it a practical compression route in real vision systems ([lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation](https://www.lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation)).

**Beyond compression — knowledge transfer and refinement.** Subsequent work in the corpus shows that distillation can improve a student *even when the student has the same capacity as the teacher*, indicating that the supervisory signal acts as a regularizer and knowledge-refinement mechanism in addition to compression ([proceedings.mlr.press/v80/furlanello18a](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/furlanello18a/furlanello18a.pdf); [group.iiis.tsinghua.edu.cn/~maks/publications/pdf/Self-distillation.pdf](http://group.iiis.tsinghua.edu.cn/~maks/publications/pdf/Self-distillation.pdf)).

This is the original setting introduced by Hinton et al.: the student is trained to reproduce the teacher's *output logits* (after temperature scaling), aligning the full class-conditional distribution rather than only the arg-max label ([arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531); [lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation](https://www.lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation)).

report that this single technique delivered significant gains on MNIST and a large-scale acoustic-modelling task, establishing logits-based distillation as the canonical KD baseline ([arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531)).

Romero et al.'s *FitNets: Hints for Thin Deep Nets* addresses this by training a "thin and deep" student using not only the teacher's outputs but also *hints* — feature maps from selected intermediate teacher layers — as additional supervision ([arxiv.org/pdf/1412.6550](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1412.6550)).

Their explicit motivation is to "address the network compression problem by taking advantage of depth": by guiding a deeper but narrower student with intermediate teacher features, FitNets exploits representational depth more effectively than purely logits-based methods ([arxiv.org/pdf/1412.6550](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1412.6550)).

(feature-based) operate in this regime, the former on small-image and acoustic data and the latter explicitly on visual benchmarks via thin deep students guided by wider teachers ([arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531); [arxiv.org/pdf/1412.6550](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1412.6550)).

- **Born-Again Neural Networks** (Furlanello et al., ICML 2018) provide "empirical rigor, providing several experiments aimed at understanding the efficacy of self-distillation," showing that a student with capacity equal to the teacher's can in fact *outperform* the teacher when trained with a KD objective alone ([proceedings.mlr.press/v80/furlanello18a](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/furlanello18a/furlanello18a.pdf)).

- **Zhang et al.'s self-distillation framework** proposes a "general training framework named self distillation, which notably enhances the performance (accuracy) of convolutional neural networks," further evidencing that the gain is not specific to any single architecture and is observable in the visual domain ([group.iiis.tsinghua.edu.cn/~maks/publications/pdf/Self-distillation.pdf](http://group.iiis.tsinghua.edu.cn/~maks/publications/pdf/Self-distillation.pdf)).

Together, these results reframe KD: it is not merely a compression device but a *learning* mechanism that improves the same model through richer supervision ([proceedings.mlr.press/v80/furlanello18a](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/furlanello18a/furlanello18a.pdf); [group.iiis.tsinghua.edu.cn/~maks/publications/pdf/Self-distillation.pdf](http://group.iiis.tsinghua.edu.cn/~maks/publications/pdf/Self-distillation.pdf)).

The supplied corpus acknowledges that KD "supports vision, language, and multi-teacher use cases" at the level of practical motivation ([lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation](https://www.lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation)).

A dedicated source on multi-teacher distillation in the supplied set (the NeurIPS 2024 talk on "Multi-Teacher Distillation: An Ensemble-Then-Distill Approach") falls outside the pre-June 2021 publication window required by this survey, so the present synthesis treats multi-teacher KD as a documented research direction in the broader landscape but does not draw pre-2021 technical claims from it ([neurips.cc/virtual/2024/106613](https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/106613)).

*Hinton et al.* establish the soft-target / logits-based distillation mechanism and demonstrate its practical value on both vision-style (MNIST) and non-vision (acoustic) tasks ([arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531)).

*Romero et al.* extend the method to intermediate representations via hints, broadening the transferable signal beyond the output layer and explicitly targeting thin-but-deep students for visual compression ([arxiv.org/pdf/1412.6550](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1412.6550)).

*Furlanello et al.* and *Zhang et al.* then show that, when teacher and student are identical, distillation still improves performance, motivating its use as a regularizer and as a generic accuracy booster, not only as a compression tool ([proceedings.mlr.press/v80/furlanello18a](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/furlanello18a/furlanello18a.pdf); [group.iiis.tsinghua.edu.cn/~maks/publications/pdf/Self-distillation.pdf](http://group.iiis.tsinghua.edu.cn/~maks/publications/pdf/Self-distillation.pdf)).

The lightweight-deployment framing offered by the lightly.ai blog is consistent with this trajectory, treating KD as a deployment-oriented technique applicable across vision, language, and multi-teacher settings ([lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation](https://www.lightly.ai/blog/knowledge-distillation)).

evidence.title: Model Compression for Dynamic Forecast Combination
evidence.abstract: The predictive advantage of combining several different predictive models is widely accepted. Particularly in time series forecasting problems, this combination is often dynamic to cope with potential non-stationary sources of variation present in the data. Despite their superior predictive performance, ensemble methods entail two main limitations: high computational costs and lack of transparency. These issues often preclude the deployment of such approaches, in favour of simpler yet more efficient and reliable ones. In this paper, we leverage the idea of model compression to address this problem in time series forecasting tasks. Model compression approaches have been mostly unexplored for forecasting. Their application in time series is challenging due to the evolving nature of the data. Further, while the literature focuses on neural networks, we apply model compression to distinct types of methods. In an extensive set of experiments, we show that compressing dynamic forecasting ensembles into an individual model leads to a comparable predictive performance and a drastic reduction in computational costs. Further, the compressed individual model with best average rank is a rule-based regression model. Thus, model compression also leads to benefits in terms of model interpretability. The experiments carried in this paper are fully reproducible.
